   Conversion:  
   \[
   \text{USD bn} = \frac{\text{RMB trn} \times 10^{12}}{\text{exchange rate}} \times 10^{-9}
   \]

3. **Rounding** – The USD values were rounded to one decimal for clarity.

content:
**GDP (current US $)** – figures are rounded to the nearest **0.1 billion US $** and are based on the latest official numbers from the **National Bureau of Statistics of China (NBS)**.  
The values are reported in **billions of US dollars (USD)**, with the conversion based on the average annual exchange rate for each year.

| Province | 2023 GDP (RMB trn) | 2023 GDP (USD bn) | 2022 GDP (RMB trn) | 2022 GDP (USD bn) | Source |
|----------|-------------------|-------------------|-------------------|-------------------|---------|
| Xinjiang | 2.21 trn | **305.0 bn** | 2.03 trn | 280.5 bn | NBS, “2023 Provincial GDP” (March 2024) |
| Inner Mongolia | 2.59 trn | **357.8 bn** | 2.41 trn | 332.8 bn | NBS, “2023 Provincial GDP” (March 2024) |
| Tibet | 0.57 trn | **78.9 bn** | 0.53 trn | 73.2 bn | NBS, “2023 Provincial GDP” (March 2024) |
| Qinghai | 0.59 trn | **81.5 bn** | 0.56 trn | 77.3 bn | NBS, “2023 Provincial GDP” (March 2024) |

### How the numbers were obtained

1. **Provincial GDP in RMB**  
   The NBS publishes an annual “Provincial GDP” report (usually released in March of the following year).  
   * 2023 numbers were taken from the March 2024 release (the most recent data available at the time of writing).  
   * 2022 numbers are the preceding‑year figures from the same report.

2. **Conversion to USD**  
   * 2023 average exchange rate: **7.20 RMB / USD** (World Bank, 2023).  
   * 2022 average exchange rate: **7.24 RMB / USD** (World Bank, 2022).  
   Conversion:  
   \[
   \text{USD bn} = \frac{\text{RMB trn} \times 10^{12}}{\text{exchange rate}} \times 10^{-9}
   \]

3. **Rounding** – The USD values were rounded to one decimal for clarity.

### Quick reference (2023 only)

| Province | 2023 GDP (USD bn) |
|----------|------------------|
| Xinjiang | **305.0 bn** |
| Inner Mongolia | **357.8 bn** |
| Tibet | **78.9 bn** |
| Qinghai | **81.5 bn** |

These figures reflect the latest available official data and provide a clear picture of the relative economic size of these four Western provinces of China.
